newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 forecast raised at Panmure Gordon. [CORRECTED 9:37 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 forecast raised at Panmure Gordon. [CORRECTED 9:37 GMT]

text.p: Panmore Gordon equity strategist Ian Williams on Friday raised his year-end target for the FTSE 100 index to 5,000 from 4,500, reflecting the market's upbeat response to monetary reforms by Britain's new Labour government.

Williams said Labour's decision to give the Bank of England independence in setting UK interest rates, which took UK shares and gilts by storm on Tuesday, was "unequivocally good news for UK asset markets."
If accompanied by an appropriate degree of fiscal tightening on personal as well as corporate taxpayers in the budget expected in July, "the outlook will become even more bullish," Williams said.

At the same time, Panmure Gordon economist Stuart Weatherby cut his year-end base rate forecast to seven percent from 7.5 percent, which he said significantly improved the domestic backdrop for gilts. He cut his year-end forecast for benchmark 10-year gilt yields to seven percent from eight percent. (Corrects name of analyst).

Williams is the first UK equity strategist to publicly raise his year-end forecast for the FTSE 100 index, following the market's buoyant reaction to Labour's landslide election victory and its shock move to grant a degree of independence to the Bank of England.

By 0826 GMT on Friday, the FTSE 100 was up 30.7 points at 4,611.1, after earlier powering to a record 4,612.1 -- some four percent above its closing level the day before the May 1 poll and 12 percent up on its level at the end of 1996.

In a research note, Williams said his previous increase to his end-1997 forecast last November had been greeted with scepticism, especially from those concerned about the impact of a possible Labour government after 18 years of market-friendly Conservative party rule.
Yet under the new Labour regime, he said he was confident Bank of England governor Eddie George would manage intrest rates to meet the government's inflation target.

The Panmure strategist said the possibility of Labour tax increases falling on the corporate sector remained a risk for the UK equity market, but he did not expect significant effects before next year or even 1999.

Williams said that on his central projection of eight percent dividend growth this year -- and assuming seven percent gilt yields -- a gilt-equity yield ratio of 2.1 times would produce a FTSE 100 level of over 5,000.
